input_analysis: Repository scan found no existing product web app; the second pilot reuses the isolated Python standard-library HTTP pattern established by the first pilot while covering a different form-submission workflow.
key_decisions: Use Python http.server and unittest so the pilot adds no external runtime dependency.
Store submissions server-side in memory behind a threading.Lock because the validation target is local workflow continuity, not durable data.
Generate opaque thanks-page ids with secrets.token_urlsafe so URLs do not expose user input.
Escape name and message with html.escape before rendering the thanks page.
Use real HTTP requests in tests so QA evidence follows the same boundary as a user journey.

key_scenarios: feedback form and thanks page are verified through real localhost HTTP requests
tradeoff_points: standard-library HTTP keeps runtime dependencies low while preserving user-journey evidence

key_scenarios: thanks page renders submitted name and message without executing user content
tradeoff_points: server-side escaping is simple and sufficient for the isolated pilot

key_scenarios: invalid feedback submissions remain visible in default HTTP access logs
tradeoff_points: default logging is enough for the pilot and avoids introducing logging dependencies

option_analysis.summary: Use an isolated Python standard-library app for the pilot.
option_analysis.tradeoff: Lower product realism than a full browser app, but provides deterministic real HTTP evidence without stack introduction.

option_analysis.summary: Introduce a frontend framework and build a browser app.
option_analysis.tradeoff: More UI realism, but adds dependency and setup noise unrelated to standard-chain handoff validation.

option_analysis.summary: Only write canonical artifacts without executable code.
option_analysis.tradeoff: Exercises validators but fails the direct-evidence requirement for feature delivery.

modules.name: feedback thanks example app
modules.responsibility: serve the feedback form, validate submissions, store valid submissions in memory, and render escaped thanks pages

data_architecture.summary: Valid feedback submissions are stored in an in-memory dictionary behind a threading lock; no durable storage or external datasource is introduced.
storage_decisions: Use process-local in-memory storage because the pilot validates standard-chain flow, not persistence.
data_flows: POST /feedback validates form data, stores escaped-source values under an opaque id, and redirects to GET /thanks?id=<id>
data_architecture.consistency_strategy: A threading.Lock guards submission storage during local ThreadingHTTPServer tests.

cross_cutting_concerns.decision: No authentication is required for the feedback pilot; anonymous form submission is intentional.
Blank fields, malformed Content-Length, oversized bodies, missing ids, and unknown ids return readable errors.
Invalid submissions keep default HTTP access-log observability.
The app introduces no external configuration; runtime remains standard-library only.

planning_constraints.description: Keep the pilot on Python standard-library HTTP and unittest without introducing external runtime dependencies.

risks.description: In-memory submission storage is not durable and is only suitable for the isolated pilot.
Invalid submissions must remain observable without adding a logging dependency.

risk_response.architecture_response: Keep storage explicitly scoped to the local pilot and document rollback as removing the isolated example.
risk_response.escalation_path: If durable storage becomes a requirement, return to design before implementation.

risk_response.architecture_response: Use default HTTP access logs and cover invalid submissions in tests.
risk_response.escalation_path: If richer audit semantics are required, escalate to design for logging architecture.
